slot.brief: Asymmetric ether reacted with excess vs one equivalent HI — give the products in each case and note SN1 vs SN2 pathway.

stem: 2-Methoxy-2-methylpropane reacts with one equivalent or with excess concentrated HI. Which option gives the products and cleavage pathways?
options: One equivalent: 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol (SN1); excess: 2-iodo-2-methylpropane, iodomethane and water (SN1, then SN2 at methyl).
One equivalent: 1-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol (SN2); excess: 1-iodo-2-methylpropane, iodomethane and water (SN2 at both carbons).
One equivalent: 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol (SN2); excess: 2-iodo-2-methylpropane, iodomethane and water (SN2 at both carbons).
One equivalent: iodomethane and 2-methylpropan-2-ol (SN2); excess: iodomethane, 2-methylpropene and water (SN1).

verdicts.working: Protonation of the ether is followed by cleavage at the tertiary carbon via SN1, giving 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol. Excess HI converts methanol to iodomethane and water.

working:
Cleavage occurs at the tertiary carbon: $\text{(CH}_3)_3\text{C–OCH}_3+\text{HI}\to\text{(CH}_3)_3\text{C–I}+\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ (SN1).\nExcess HI: $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}+\text{HI}\to\text{CH}_3\text{I}+\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (SN2 at methyl).

Independent check: Protonation of the ether is followed by cleavage at the tertiary carbon via SN1, giving 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol. Excess HI converts methanol to iodomethane and water.
solution:
Protonation of the ether is followed by cleavage at the tertiary carbon via $S_N1$:
$$\text{(CH}_3)_3\text{C–OCH}_3+\text{HI}\to\text{(CH}_3)_3\text{C–I}+\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$
With excess HI, methanol undergoes $S_N2$ cleavage at methyl: $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}+\text{HI}\to\text{CH}_3\text{I}+\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Thus, the products and pathways match (A).
